page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.1-16 is a flexible standard-tier virtual machine instance designed for memory-weighted general computing. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8358 processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.6 GHz. Compute capacity consists of 1 dedicated physical core mapped across 2 hardware execution threads, exposing 2 vCPUs in total. The processor operates without supplemental hardware acceleration frameworks such as AVX-512, AMX, or hardware-assisted virtualization flags enabled.

The compute resources are paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. This elevated memory-to-vCPU proportion positions the profile closer to memory-oriented configurations rather than strictly balanced tiers. The instance lacks local storage, necessitating external network-attached block volumes for persistent disk drives and operational file storage. It does not integrate dedicated GPU hardware, operating strictly on CPU compute pipelines, and includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for ingress and egress routing.

In qualitative efficiency terms, the shape provides dedicated core isolation and a generous memory pool at a compact core count, eliminating the overhead of paying for unneeded processor threads when application memory footprints drive instance requirements. VM.Standard3.Flex.1-16 is best suited for memory-intensive web caching, lightweight relational databases, background batch processors, internal tool hosting, and microservices requiring substantial memory overhead without heavy parallel CPU requirements.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard3.Flex.1-16 is a standard-tier virtual machine instance configured with an Intel Xeon Platinum 8358 processor on the x86_64 architecture running at 2.6 GHz. It provides 1 dedicated physical core that supplies 2 vCPUs via multithreading, alongside 16.0 GB of system memory. This establishes an above-average memory allocation of 8.0 GB per core. The server configuration includes no integrated GPU hardware and has no local ephemeral storage, requiring remote block volume integration for data persistence. One complimentary public IPv4 address is bundled with the instance. Delivering isolated compute execution without overprovisioning processor cores, this configuration represents a cost-efficient footprint for memory-dependent tasks. It is well matched for mid-sized caching services, small relational databases, staging environments, and memory-heavy microservices.
